personalInfo.storyContent:
I am **Lê Trí Trung** (born 2005), Founder, Head of Technology, and Technical Business Analyst at **SynapForge Venture Studio** in Da Nang. My day-to-day work combines software requirements engineering (Karl Wiegers 3rd Ed.) with hands-on system architecture and full-stack code across web platforms, SaaS automation, and AI applications.

I study Software Engineering at **[FPT University Da Nang](/achievements?tab=education)** (**GPA 3.3/4.0 - 8.2/10.0**), represented the university in the **[International Student Exchange Programme](/achievements?tab=education)** at **TAR UMT Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia** (12/2023), hold an **IELTS 6.0** certificate (IDP Education, 04/2026), and graduated from **Phan Chau Trinh High School** with a **GPA of 9.0/10.0**.

Along the way, I won **[First Place at Hackathon Computer Vision 2026](/achievements?tab=prizes)** (FPT Education × SIT Singapore), reached the **[National Finals of InnoCodeCamp 2025](/achievements?tab=prizes)** as Team Leader and the **[National Finals of ResFres 2024](/achievements?tab=prizes)**, and co-authored an **[International Scientific Paper (ICTA 2026)](/achievements?tab=prizes)** on fine-tuning small code models to detect and patch race-condition bugs in JavaScript.

Four production systems and Technical BA specifications represent the core of my recent work:
1. **[Biensovip.com](/projects/26) (Solo Software Architect & Lead BA):** Wrote the full specification (57 Use Cases, 85 Business Rules) and built a national license plate marketplace from scratch on .NET 8 Clean Architecture. It runs on 61 PostgreSQL entity tables (<8ms GIN queries), a **1.1M+ National VPA Auction data pipeline**, a **4-Tab Finite State Machine (FSM)**, **TikTok Live 9:16 Safe-Zone Assistant & F1-F6 Soundboard**, VietQR Webhook deposit settlement (<0.5s), and a DeepSeek AI Chatbot.
2. **[BrandHub](/projects/14) (Tech Lead, Solutions Architect & Lead BA):** Structured 109 raw agency requests into **141 Atomic Functional Requirements** (Karl Wiegers Zero-Manage Rule), designed a 7-microservice multichannel publishing platform (Spring Cloud Gateway, RabbitMQ DLQ with 0% message loss, Java 21, Python GraphRAG), a **79-screen React Native mobile app**, and **2,500+ test cases / 320+ Playwright E2E test suites** (live at `brandhub.id.vn`).
3. **[The MC Hub](/projects/11) (CEO, Tech Lead & Lead BA):** Led a 6-engineer team building an AI voice training platform (React 19 + Spring Boot 3.3 + Python FastAPI & **10-Metric Acoustic DSP + Whisper Engine**), authored **116 Atomic FRs** and 139 Visual Paradigm UML diagrams, and onboarded 87 professional MCs with paid subscriptions in the first month.
4. **[Live TikTok 3D Interactive Game Ecosystem](/projects/30) (`cungchuaonline`):** Built a 12-game real-time 9:16 3D TikTok Live suite (Cúng Chùa Online 3D, Cuộc Đua Kỳ Thú 3D, AdminTong with 21 ApexCharts) backed by 193/193 passing automated tests.

Outside of software engineering, I have hosted **50+ university and tech events as an MC (600–1,000+ attendees)**, served as Head Referee for FPTU AI & Robotics 2025, and founded **[The Dreamers Charity Organization](/activities)** (30+ members) to run coding workshops and community programs for underprivileged children in Central Vietnam.

projectItems.description:
A full-stack job search platform built with a 6-person Agile team. I handled the backend architecture: designing RESTful APIs in Java Spring Boot, managing relational data in SQL Server, and integrating an AI chatbot for resume feedback and job matching.

My main contributions included the JWT authentication flow (login/register), the job posting and application APIs, and the Git branching workflow (feature branches + pull requests) that kept our 6-person team's commits clean across 4 months of development.

The frontend is deployed on Vercel with job filtering and application tracking.
projectItems.challenge: Build a job platform where candidates can search and apply while getting AI resume feedback, while keeping a 6-person student team coordinated on a shared codebase over 4 months.
highlights: Designed and built RESTful APIs in Java Spring Boot with relational data in SQL Server
Built JWT authentication (login/register) and role-based access from scratch
Set up a Git branching workflow (feature branch + pull request) across a 6-person team for 4 months
Integrated an AI chatbot to provide resume tips and job recommendations

projectItems.description:
Led a 4-person team to build an e-commerce website for a bakery, covering the product catalog, shopping cart, order management, and customer accounts. I built the Java Servlets backend, designed the SQL Server schema, and divided tasks across weekly sprints.

We also integrated an AI customer support chatbot via API, Google Maps API for store directions, and Google OAuth login. The frontend uses plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to keep pages fast and simple to debug.

As my first project as team lead, it taught me how to scope features for a fixed deadline, resolve merge conflicts before submission, and ship a working end-to-end application.
projectItems.challenge: My first team lead role: shipping a complete bakery e-commerce site (catalog, cart, orders, customer accounts) with a 4-person team on a fixed semester deadline.
highlights: Built the backend in Java Servlets and designed the SQL Server database schema from scratch
Coordinated a 4-person team using weekly sprint task breakdowns
Integrated an AI support chatbot, Google Maps API store locator, and Google OAuth login
Resolved merge conflicts under deadline pressure and delivered the finished site on schedule

projectItems.description:
I founded and run The Dreamers, a student charity group at FPT University Da Nang. We organize basic coding workshops, communication sessions, and charity visits for orphaned children and underprivileged youth in Central Vietnam.

I coordinate member recruitment, plan our semester roadmap, partner with local shelters, and manage accounting for our fundraising campaigns.

Since launching, our team has organized Tốt Hy Vọng, Vòng vào Mộng mơ, Dream High, and a Charity Music Performance concert. We are also building an internal backend in Java Spring Boot to track member records and event history.
projectItems.challenge: Keeping a student charity group active across multiple semesters by recruiting new cohorts, running transparent fundraising, and building an internal backend to track members and events.
highlights: Founded and coordinate 30+ members across recruitment, event planning, and charity fundraising
Organized 4 major community programs: Tốt Hy Vọng, Vòng vào Mộng mơ, Dream High, and Charity Music Performance
Building an internal Java Spring Boot backend to manage member and event records

projectItems.description:
A small utility built in 10 days to automate repetitive web form submissions and remove manual data entry for batch inputs.

The backend uses Node.js to drive form interactions via DOM scripting, paired with a React interface where users upload CSV or JSON files, preview rows, and trigger batch submissions. I also added handlers for validation delays and dynamically rendered form fields.

Building this gave me practical experience with browser DOM timing and async scripting, which later proved useful when writing Playwright E2E test suites.
projectItems.challenge: Automate batch data entry for web forms within a 10-day timeline while handling validation delays and dynamically rendered input fields.
highlights: Built a Node.js DOM scripting engine to automate form filling and submission
Created a React interface for uploading CSV/JSON files, previewing rows, and running batch jobs
Handled validation delays and dynamically rendered form fields
Completed solo from start to finish in 10 days

projectItems.description:
An online bookstore built on the OutSystems low-code platform during my OJT internship at FPT Software Da Nang.

The application covers standard e-commerce flows: a searchable and filterable book catalog, shopping cart, order checkout, and an inventory admin panel. Working in OutSystems taught me how to structure data models, UI logic, and REST integrations using FSoft's 4-Layer Architecture standard.

The live demo is hosted on OutSystems Cloud.
projectItems.challenge: Learn OutSystems Reactive Web and ship a complete e-commerce application following 4-Layer Architecture during my internship training at FPT Software.
highlights: Built the full bookstore flow: catalog with search and filter, cart, order management, and inventory admin panel
Applied OutSystems 4-Layer Architecture for data modeling, UI logic, and API integration
Deployed a public live demo on OutSystems Cloud

projectItems.description:
A frontend clone of the TikTok web interface built during the F8 React course.

My goal was to practice breaking a complex UI into reusable React components (Sidebar, VideoFeed, UserCard, ActionBar) with clear props, state, and side-effect boundaries. While building it, I wrote custom hooks (such as `useDebounce` for search), configured multi-page routing with React Router, used CSS Modules for scoped styling, and wrote responsive layouts without a UI component library.

This project gave me a solid React foundation before moving on to larger systems like Job Finder, The MC Hub, and Biensovip.
projectItems.challenge: Rebuild the interactive TikTok web interface from scratch using React and CSS Modules without relying on pre-built UI component libraries.
highlights: Structured the interface into reusable components: Sidebar, VideoFeed, UserCard, and ActionBar
Wrote custom hooks (`useDebounce`), wired search API calls, and used React Router with CSS Modules
Built a responsive layout across screen sizes without external UI libraries

projectItems.description:
This portfolio website. I designed and coded it from scratch around the **Robin Tactile Notebook & Pixel Scrapbook** aesthetic: warm lined notebook paper (`#F9F6F1`), a retro pixel-art nameplate, washi-taped polaroid frames, yellow/green/pink stickers, and tabbed folder dossiers.

The app runs on **React 19** and **React Router v6**, with instant Vietnamese/English switching, a `Ctrl+K` Command Palette, interactive skill filtering, and a Recruiter Match widget.

All project entries, blog posts, and certificates are decoupled into `src/data.js` and locale files (`vi.json` / `en.json`), paired with a custom `SeoHeadManager` that injects dynamic meta tags and Schema.org `@graph` JSON-LD per route.
projectItems.challenge: Design a personal portfolio that feels like a tactile engineering notebook while organizing 30+ projects, 48 certificates, and 13 technical blog posts with fast load times and clean SEO.
highlights: Custom Robin Tactile Notebook & Pixel Scrapbook design system built without off-the-shelf templates
Data-driven content architecture in data.js with full Vietnamese and English localization
Dynamic SeoHeadManager, Schema.org JSON-LD (@graph), sitemap.xml, and llms.txt
Route-level code-splitting, Cloudinary image optimization, and prefers-reduced-motion support

projectItems.description:
A full-stack internal management web app for a bakery, built solo for a university course with the scope of a real store back-office: ingredient inventory tracking, sales logs, order processing, and a customer list connected via REST APIs.

The backend uses Java Spring Boot and MySQL, serving a React frontend deployed on Vercel. I handled the database schema, REST endpoints, React components, and deployment configuration myself.

Building the entire stack solo helped me trace how data moves from a UI form submission down to SQL queries and back.
projectItems.challenge: Design and build a complete bakery back-office system (inventory, sales, orders, customers) solo, covering MySQL schema design, Spring Boot APIs, and the React frontend.
highlights: Designed the REST API and MySQL relational schema solo across 4 management modules
Built the Java Spring Boot backend and React frontend deployed on Vercel
Handled the full workflow from database modeling to API integration and deployment

projectItems.description:
An AI voice and public speaking training platform (React 19 + Java Spring Boot 3.3 + Python FastAPI) that generated revenue in its first month: 87 MCs onboarded and 20 paid subscriptions (~4M VND) across Basic and Full tiers.

We built a Python FastAPI, Librosa, and OpenAI Whisper microservice that extracts 10 acoustic metrics (F0 pitch, HNR, Jitter, Shimmer, speaking pace, pauses, filler words) to score 101 practice exercises, 40 theory lessons, and 4 courses across 6 MC categories.

I led our 6-person team from initial specification (116 Atomic FRs and 139 Visual Paradigm diagrams) to production in 6 months.
projectItems.challenge: Build and launch a commercial AI voice training platform with real-time acoustic scoring in 6 months with a 6-person engineering team.
highlights: Onboarded 87 MCs and recorded 20 paid transactions (~4M VND) in the first month after launch
Built a Python FastAPI + Whisper + Librosa microservice evaluating pronunciation, intonation, pace, and pauses across 101 exercises
Led a 6-person team from Karl Wiegers SRS specification (116 Atomic FRs) to CI/CD deployment on Vercel and Render
Tech stack: Java 21 Spring Boot 3.3, React 19, Python FastAPI, Whisper, MongoDB, Redis

projectItems.description:
A Vietnamese agricultural marketplace connecting farmers, suppliers, and buyers with product listings, orders, reviews, and notifications. It began as a mobile course project (PRM393) using a Flutter app and an Express.js/MongoDB backend with JWT auth.

After the course, our team built an expanded web and backend version for a startup competition: a Next.js + TypeScript frontend (Radix UI, TanStack Query, Sentry, and Mapbox/d3-geo farm maps) paired with a NestJS + TypeORM backend and a formal Vietnamese business proposal.
projectItems.challenge: Evolve a semester mobile project (PRM393) into a multi-platform web and mobile architecture (Next.js + Flutter + NestJS) ready for a university startup competition.
highlights: Track 1 (mobile): Flutter mobile app with an Express.js/MongoDB backend and JWT authentication
Track 2 (web expansion): Next.js + TypeScript frontend with Mapbox/d3-geo farm mapping and a NestJS + TypeORM backend
Prepared a full Vietnamese startup proposal for the agricultural marketplace model

projectItems.description:
A multichannel brand content management platform for agencies publishing across 5 social networks (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Threads, and Zalo), supporting content drafting, approval workflows, AI Brand Voice modeling, campaign scheduling, and automated publishing.

Built on a 7-microservice architecture: API Gateway (Spring Cloud Gateway, WebFlux, JWT + Redis auth and rate-limiting), business-service (Spring Boot 3.3.5, Java 21) for multi-tenant workspaces and campaigns, publisher-service consuming from RabbitMQ with Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) exponential backoff to prevent dropped posts, and an AI service (Python FastAPI, RAG & GraphRAG with ChromaDB and Neo4j). Includes a React 18 + TypeScript dashboard, a 79-screen Expo/React Native mobile app, and 2,500+ test cases.
projectItems.challenge: Publish scheduled posts across 5 social networks without losing messages when third-party APIs fail, while structuring 109 raw agency requests into 141 Atomic FRs for a 5-engineer team.
highlights: Designed a 7-microservice architecture: API Gateway (Spring Cloud Gateway), business-service (Java 21), publisher-service (RabbitMQ DLQ), and AI service (FastAPI GraphRAG)
Configured Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) exponential retry to keep message loss at 0% during social API outages
Used RAG & GraphRAG (ChromaDB + Neo4j) to model Brand Voice and surface campaign trends
Shipped a React 18 + TypeScript dashboard, a 79-screen React Native mobile app, and 320+ Playwright E2E test files

projectItems.challenge: Migrate a content-heavy static HTML tourism site into a modern React 19 application while keeping Markdown rendering safe and image-heavy pages fast.
highlights: Migrated from static HTML to React 19 + Vite with site-wide image lazy-loading
Sanitized dynamic Markdown content with DOMPurify to prevent XSS issues
Added a lightweight 3D hero element using Three.js and React Three Fiber
Styled responsive layouts with Tailwind CSS 4 and Framer Motion transitions

Built a React 18 + TypeScript frontend with Monaco Editor, Mermaid diagrams, Recharts, and PDF export

postItems.title: Teaching a 1.5B-Parameter Model to Fix JavaScript Concurrency Bugs
postItems.excerpt: Inside ThreadLearn: fine-tuning Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B with QLoRA, pairing it with a BM25 + AST RAG pipeline, and why a small model beat GPT-3.5-turbo on a focused domain.
postItems.content:
JavaScript runs on a single-threaded event loop while handling overlapping asynchronous tasks through callbacks, Promises, and async/await. That gap between a single execution thread and interleaved I/O tasks creates a stubborn class of defects: **concurrency bugs**. In the NodeCB study (ASE 2017), which examined 57 real-world bugs across 53 Node.js repositories, 93% caused severe failures such as server crashes, corrupted state, or hung processes. Worse, they rarely show up in isolated unit tests.

A classic example is two requests reading and updating inventory at the same time:

```javascript
const stock = await db.getStock(productId);   // both requests read stock = 1
await db.setStock(productId, stock - 1);       // both requests write stock = 0
// 2 units sold when inventory only had 1 (race condition)
```

Static linters like ESLint can flag suspicious patterns, but they don't generate patches. Calling large commercial APIs like GPT-4 adds per-request cost, requires external network access, and still hallucinates Node.js concurrency primitives. For **ThreadLearn** (our WDP301 capstone project at FPT University), my two teammates and I took a more targeted route: fine-tune a compact 1.5B model (`Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B`) specifically on JavaScript concurrency fixes, then ground its API usage with a lightweight RAG pipeline.

## Why a 1.5B model instead of GPT-4

We had three practical constraints: inference cost, latency, and running offline inside firewalled company networks. We chose **Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B** because it fits comfortably in 8GB of GPU VRAM while already knowing JavaScript syntax from pretraining. We fine-tuned it with **QLoRA** (loading weights in 4-bit NF4 and training a rank-16 LoRA adapter, roughly 0.5% of total parameters) on two free Kaggle T4 GPUs in about two hours.

My teammate Ha Van An curated the 783 buggy/fixed code pairs from GitHub and ran the QLoRA training. I owned the **RAG retrieval pipeline, static race-condition detector, and FastAPI inference server**.

## Designing RAG for code: BM25 + AST over Vector Search

When patching JavaScript, developers care about exact API identifiers like `Promise.all`, `setTimeout`, or `fs.appendFile`. Vector databases (FAISS, Chroma) require a 500MB+ embedding model and often rank loosely related prose above the exact function signature. By contrast, **BM25** indexes our 2,050-document knowledge base in under 500ms on CPU and excels at exact token matching.

The catch is that standard BM25 tokenizers split CamelCase identifiers poorly: `setTimeout` turns into `["set", "timeout"]` and `fetchAllUsers` becomes `["fetch", "all", "users"]`. My first attempt used regex splitting, which still mangled method names when extracting search queries from buggy code.

To fix that, I used **esprima to parse the input JavaScript into an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)** and extracted only `Identifier` tokens (function and variable names), ignoring language keywords (`async`, `await`, `for`):

```python
script = esprima.parseScript(code, options={"tolerant": True, "tokens": True})
for tok in script.tokens:
    if tok.type == "Identifier" and tok.value not in _JS_STOPWORDS:
        result.append(tok.value)
```

On `fs.appendFile(logPath, data)`, the regex tokenizer produced `"fs append file path data"` (losing `appendFile`), whereas AST extraction preserved `"fs appendFile logPath data"`. Keeping exact API identifiers intact noticeably improved top-3 document retrieval.

## Evaluation Results

We evaluated the system on 20 hand-crafted test cases spanning 8 concurrency bug categories (race conditions, event loop blocking, unhandled rejections, callback hell, zalgo, context loss, etc.) using Fix-Pattern Scoring:

| Method | Pass | Partial | Fail | Pass Rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GPT-3.5-turbo zero-shot | 6 | 11 | 3 | 30% |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B (base, no fine-tune) | 8 | 9 | 3 | 40% |
| ThreadLearn RAW (fine-tuned, no RAG) | 14 | 6 | 0 | 70% |
| **ThreadLearn + RAG** | **15** | **5** | **0** | **75%** |

![Ablation chart](https://res.cloudinary.com/dvwt6npcl/image/upload/f_auto,q_auto/v1783871855/my-website/assets/blog/threadlearn/fig_ablation.png)

### Benchmark 2: 30 real-world bugs from GitHub Issues

On 30 real concurrency bugs collected from production npm packages, ThreadLearn + RAG scored **73.3% (22/30)**, compared to **65.0% (19.5/30)** for GPT-3.5-turbo running with the same retrieval pipeline. Full test cases are documented in `server/tests/real_world/README.md`.

### What the numbers show

QLoRA fine-tuning drove a **+30 percentage point** jump (40% to 70%), teaching the model structural fix patterns from 783 examples. Adding AST + BM25 RAG contributed another **+5 percentage points** (70% to 75%) on cases requiring specific Node.js API signatures. Across all 20 cases, the model produced syntactically valid code.

**Remaining weak spots** were Zalgo (0/1), Double Callback (0/1), and Buffer Leak (0/1), which had very few examples in our training set. Event Loop Blocking reached **100% (5/5)**.

![Per-category breakdown](https://res.cloudinary.com/dvwt6npcl/image/upload/f_auto,q_auto/v1783871858/my-website/assets/blog/threadlearn/fig_category.png)

## Key Takeaways

A 1.5B model fine-tuned on a narrow task and paired with AST-aware keyword retrieval can beat a general-purpose model 125x its size on that specific task, while running locally on consumer hardware. For source code retrieval, BM25 + AST identifier extraction is faster, simpler, and more accurate than dense vector embeddings.

---

*Team contributions: **Le Tri Trung** (AI2: RAG Pipeline, FastAPI Server, Static Race Detector) · Ha Van An (AI1: Dataset Collection, QLoRA Fine-tuning) · Nguyen Thi Thuy Hoai (Model Evaluation & Paper Writing). FPT University Da Nang.*

Code, dataset, and paper: [github.com/ThreadLearn/ThreadLearn_AI_Trainning](https://github.com/ThreadLearn/ThreadLearn_AI_Trainning). Full PDF: `/d/FPT/threadlearn_paper-full.pdf`. Visual demo: [github.com/ThreadLearn/ThreadLearn-AI-Visual](https://github.com/ThreadLearn/ThreadLearn-AI-Visual).
